panels.description: Sampled peer RTT and media RTT p95 over five minutes. Media combines ingress and egress observations. No observations or unavailable scrape data produces a gap.

panels.description: Mean sampled ingress and egress loss fractions over five minutes. Samples can include peer and stream reports and are not weighted by packet volume. A gap means no observations or unavailable scrape data.

panels.description: Mean sampled peer egress bandwidth estimate over five minutes. This is an observation average and does not describe the worst receiver. A gap means no BWE observations or unavailable scrape data.

panels.description: Mean sampled remote egress jitter in raw RTP timestamp units. Values can mix codec clock rates and are not milliseconds. A gap means no jitter observations or unavailable scrape data.

panels.title: Decoder Refreshes
panels.description: Decoder-refresh RTP packets by source or RID scope. Aggregate counts do not identify a frozen receiver. Inspect its selected encoding and packet timestamps in User Diagnostics.

panels.title: Keyframe Recovery Outcomes
panels.description: Keyframe tracker forwards, coalesced requests, retries and requests cleared by decoder refreshes. These event rates do not form a per-request success ratio.

panels.title: Generic NACK Feedback
panels.description: Generic NACK events sent to publishers or received from subscribers. Events can request multiple packets and are not a packet-loss percentage.

panels.title: Publisher RTX Received
panels.description: Authenticated repair packets accepted from publishers after de-RTX. No subscriber retransmission count or repair success ratio is inferred.

panels.title: RTCP Ingress Budget Drops
panels.description: Candidate RTCP datagrams rejected by the per-session ingress byte budget. This is a server protection event, not a measured network-loss rate.

panels.title: Output Budget Exhaustions
panels.description: RTC session drains that exceeded a packet or payload-byte budget. Exhaustion rolls back the drain and closes that session.

panels.title: Sessions Closed by Output Budget
panels.description: RTC sessions closed because an output drain exceeded its budget. Correlate with transport disconnects and session logs.
Total rate of committed receiver video route degradation, pause and resume transitions.
panels.title: Video Route Transitions/s

panels.description: Rate of committed receiver video routes entering a policy pause. Inspect user diagnostics for budget, layout or layer availability reasons.
panels.title: Policy Pauses/s

panels.description: Rate of committed receiver video routes clearing an existing policy pause.
panels.title: Policy Resumes/s

panels.description: Average rate of committed receiver video route transitions by outcome over the selected time range.
panels.title: Video Route Transition Mix

panels.description: Rate of committed receiver video route degradation, pause and resume transitions over time.
panels.title: Video Route Transition Rates

panels.description: Compares accepted encoding-selector updates with committed receiver video route transitions and policy pauses.
panels.title: Selector Updates and Route Transitions

options.content:
- **degraded**: an unpaused route switched to a lower estimated bitrate.
- **paused**: a route entered a policy pause for budget, layout, unavailable layers or a receiver limit.
- **resumed**: a route cleared its policy pause.

These are committed transition rates. Zero transitions does not prove that routes are delivering. Open **User Diagnostics** for the selected encoding, pause reason, pending upgrade and packet timestamps.

panels.title: How to Read Receiver Budget Policy

panels.description: The volume of actual audio/video data entering (ingress) and leaving (egress) the server. Egress is usually much higher as one person broadcasting is sent to many viewers.
panels.title: RTP Payload Bitrate

panels.description: RTP fan-out operations to local RTC consumers, intra-node relay workers or packet sinks. Destination labels identify delivery paths rather than physical network interfaces.
panels.title: Forwarded Packets by Destination

panels.description: Shows which internal logic paths are being used to move data. This helps developers verify that the 'fast path' is being used for media instead of slower 'fallback' paths.
panels.title: RTC Datagram Routing Paths

panels.description: RTC UDP datagrams rejected before session delivery, by no_user, malformed, source_rate_limited or recent_miss_cache. These counters do not measure receiver packet loss or network congestion.
panels.title: Ingress Routing Rejections

panels.description: Measures how hard the server is working to find valid recipients for incoming media. Sudden spikes here can indicate high CPU usage and potential lag.
panels.title: Routing Pressure

panels.description: Transport route-control outcomes. Layer filtering and route-gated relay drops are distinct from forwarded or coalesced keyframe requests.
panels.title: Route Control Outcomes

panels.description: summarizes current relay pressure rates from bounded mailbox and remote-control signals
panels.title: Relay Pressure Rates

panels.description: tracks average bounded relay mailbox depth from sampled packet-loop drains
panels.title: Relay Mailbox Depth

panels.description: shows accepted plus overloaded plus closed relay enqueue outcomes split by target loop
panels.title: Relay Enqueue Outcomes

panels.description: compares relay drain throughput with cap hits to show when loops leave queued packets for a later turn
panels.title: Relay Drain Pressure

panels.description: Remote-source control commands dropped before enqueue, split into keyframe and packet_gate commands. This metric does not identify the drop reason.
panels.title: Remote Control Drops by Command
